expectations.text: States that response rate is undefined for the open-link channels (newsletter, docs banner, Discord) because they have no denominator.
expectations.evidence: 'Three of your four channels have no valid response rate... Newsletter, docs banner and Discord are open links'.

expectations.text: Rejects the 20-30% threshold as having no methodological source, and states that response rate predicts bias poorly.
expectations.evidence: 'No methodological source backs it. Response rate predicts bias poorly.'

expectations.text: Reports a funnel per channel instead: views where known, starts, completes, kept.
expectations.evidence: 'Report the funnel instead: views where known, starts, completes, kept.'

expectations.text: Identifies the random first-launch prompt as the only channel with a denominator and reports its invited (2,000), started and completed (240) counts.
expectations.evidence: 'Calibration (random) | 240 | 2,000 invited, 240 completed (12%). Add started.'

expectations.text: Uses the random group as a calibration sample, comparing its answers question by question with the self-selected respondents to measure drift.
expectations.evidence: 'Show the random group (n=240) beside the self-selected group (n=1,270) on every core question.'

expectations.text: States that the random group's 12% completion still carries nonresponse bias, and that its invited-to-completed rate is printed beside any rung-2 number.
expectations.evidence: 'Always print the 12% beside the number. A random invitation with 88% non-completion still carries nonresponse bias.'

expectations.text: Publishes the source mix (completes per channel) in the methodology.
expectations.evidence: Funnel and source mix table with share of 1,510.

expectations.text: Writes a bias sentence naming who the sample over-represents (newsletter subscribers, engaged community members).
expectations.evidence: 'Respondents over-represent engaged Quillhaven community members: 84% came from our newsletter, docs and Discord.'

expectations.text: Does not recommend a gift card draw as the fix, noting that draw effects on completes are small and inconsistent and that the real cost is compliance and fraud screening.
expectations.evidence: 'Draw effects are small and inconsistent... compliance cost... attracts bots'.

expectations.text: Does not declare the survey worthless; states that results are publishable at the respondents rung with n and wording.
expectations.evidence: 'The survey is usable.' and 'Rung 1, all respondents... Always allowed, with n and exact wording.'

expectations.text: States that self-selected and random-group results are shown apart wherever they differ.
expectations.evidence: 'Where they differ, show both and say so.'
